channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Analyst traces history of vice presidents in Sierra Leone
item.description: A public policy analyst examines why the vice presidency has never led to the presidency since independence.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: The practice of burning wood for charcoal is destroying economic trees and increasing greenhouse gas emissions.

item.title: Libyan experts propose unified national framework for medical training
item.description: A Benghazi symposium recommended continuous evaluation of trainees and a single national certification for specialists.

item.title: Cyril Ramaphosa turns 74 during Silicon Valley working visit
item.description: South Africa's president marks his 74th birthday in California on a working visit focused on artificial intelligence.

item.title: Benin institute urges leaders to put human dignity before growth figures
item.description: The IAJP, a Catholic justice and peace institute, calls for policies on purchasing power, social justice and essential services, not infrastructure alone.

item.title: Plateau records 5,457 suspected diabetes cases in nine months
item.description: The nine-month total already comes close to the 5,546 suspected cases the state recorded across the whole of 2025.

item.title: ACEP Burkina opens two service points near Ouagadougou markets
item.description: The microfinance institution opened the counters at Sankar-Yaaré and 10 Yaar on Monday, 16 November 2026, to bring its services closer to market users.

item.title: Tunisia faces Libya in Tripoli for Africa Cup of Nations qualifier
item.description: The national football team plays away after a previous defeat in Sfax.

item.title: Banco de Cabo Verde seeks data center maintenance
item.description: The central bank is hiring a firm to service its data center and UPS systems for 12 months.

item.title: Zambia performs first-ever cochlear implant activation at UTH
item.description: A 20-year-old patient with profound hearing loss received the country's first cochlear implant activation.

item.title: Eswatini plans more local electricity generation
item.description: Government is working on hydropower, solar and geothermal projects to cut reliance on power imported from neighbouring countries, and says regional cooperation remains essential.

item.title: Mauritius extends police commissioner's contract for one year
item.description: Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam confirmed in parliament that Rampersad Sooroojbally will stay on as the country's police chief.

item.title: Natembeya's aide in intensive care after night attack
item.description: Amos Boaz, a political ally and communication officer of Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, was attacked by unknown assailants on Monday night.

item.title: Karamoja hunger deaths prompt questions over state food relief
item.description: About 473,000 people in the subregion face high levels of acute food insecurity, according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC).

item.title: Namibia trains 32 Hai||om youth in business farming
item.description: The Hai||om San Traditional Authority aims to shift subsistence farmers to profit-driven practices and curb rural migration.

item.title: Yamoussoukro students and officials plant trees to mark peace day
item.description: Forestry officials say planting trees together builds social cohesion and restores the country's forest cover.

item.title: Swakop Uranium invests $300 million in Husab Mine expansion
item.description: The company's Industrial Heap Leach Project will add a new processing method to recover value from lower-grade uranium resources.

item.title: Cameroon hosts African customs intelligence workshop
item.description: Yaoundé is hosting a week of geospatial intelligence training for 28 customs participants from 14 countries, opened by Cameroon's customs director general.

item.title: South Sudan protests exclusion from UNISFA mandate drafting
item.description: South Sudan objected to being left out of consultations for a United Nations peacekeeping force mandate extension.

item.title: Ngaya Club wins 3-0 in Ngazidja second division
item.description: Alizé Fort and US Mbeni lead the league with 10 points each after four matches.

item.title: Ateny vows action against crimes targeting journalists
item.description: South Sudan's information minister pledged investigations following the killing of journalist Veronica Lucy Gordon.

item.title: Chad's Gondja festival spotlights second-hand clothing as a path to women's autonomy
item.description: The second edition of the Gondja festival runs from November 24 to 26 at the Talino Manu space in N'Djamena, with exhibitors presenting their goods to the public.

item.title: Fountain of Life Church removes Jimmy Odukoya as senior pastor
item.description: Trustees say they are enforcing the succession plan left by the late founder, Taiwo Odukoya, who died in 2023.

item.title: Rwanda minister accuses DRC counterpart of lying
item.description: Rwanda's Foreign Affairs Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe stated that DRC's Wagner Kayikwamba spread disinformation regarding Louise Mushikiwabo's mandate at La Francophonie.

item.title: Tunisia and Wyoming expand academic ties to energy and water
item.description: The US ambassador outlines plans for new economic and technological projects following a university exchange program started in October 2024.

item.title: TAAG adds seventh Airbus A220-300 to its fleet in Luanda
item.description: The Angolan national airline took delivery of the aircraft, registered D2-TAQ, which arrived from Canada under a leasing agreement.

item.title: Sierra Leone opens West Africa investment summit in Lungi
item.description: The three-day WAIIS 2026 gathering, which runs to November 18, has a regional investment pipeline above US$180 billion, according to organisers.

item.title: South Sudan signs sports infrastructure deal with Chinese firm
item.description: The ministry partners with Bai Chuan Water Conservancy and Electric Power Construction Company to build a national basketball stadium.

item.title: MSF reduces staff in Bunyakiri amid clashes
item.description: Médecins Sans Frontières has temporarily reduced its personnel in Bunyakiri health zone, South Kivu, due to armed confrontations.

item.title: Mozambique police urge calm as ex-presidential candidate Mondlane goes on trial
item.description: Venâncio Mondlane, who leads the ANAMOLA party, faces five charges linked to the post-election protests of late 2024 and early 2025.

item.title: Malawi school group defends exam re-marking
item.description: The Private Schools Association of Malawi says grade changes after re-marking are a standard procedure, not a conspiracy.

item.title: Nigeria's headline inflation falls to 14.06% in October
item.description: Food inflation also eased to 19.13 percent, though prices rose 0.43 percent month on month.

item.title: Front Polisario issues mobilisation call after Morocco troop movements
item.description: The independence movement accuses Morocco of massing forces near its defensive wall.

item.title: Ghana's new cedi notes spark debate over portraits
item.description: The Bank of Ghana's new currency series has ignited public discussion about replacing human faces with national symbols.

item.title: Mali's foreign minister receives Egypt's new ambassador in Bamako
item.description: Abdoulaye Diop met Al-Hassan Abou Elsaoud Abdou Soliman, who presented copies of his letters of credence on Monday, 16 November 2026.

item.title: Togo targets 1 000 vulnerable women for ID documents
item.description: The social action is part of the 2027-2029 budget-programme to reduce administrative barriers.

item.title: Rwanda to host EU migrant return hub
item.description: Five European nations will send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda starting in 2027.

item.title: Ghana's Black Challenge thrash Iraq 6-0 to reach Amputee World Cup last 16
item.description: The team finished second in Group D behind Angola, and will now face the USA on Wednesday, November 18, for a place in the quarter-finals.

item.title: Epson Tunisie plants 2 000 trees in Rafraf to reach 4 000 total
item.description: The technology firm planted trees in a forest damaged by fires during the National Tree Day celebration.

item.title: Yei records 1,918 primary candidates despite insecurity
item.description: Yei River County's Primary Eight candidates rose from 1,825 last year to 1,918 this year, even as insecurity forces some learners to sit exams elsewhere.

item.title: Murkomen tours Rome police centre as Kenya and Italy sign security deal
item.description: Kenya's interior minister toured Italian surveillance and intelligence systems before signing a cooperation agreement with Rome.

item.title: Habari Leo publishes lessons on Swahili proverb meaning
item.description: New educational columns in Tanzanian newspapers examine the literal and figurative meanings of the traditional Swahili saying.

item.title: Namibia takes over RCMRD chairmanship from Zambia
item.description: Minister Inge Zaamwani says the chairmanship will concentrate on finances, staff skills and cooperation between member states.

item.title: Tanzania's WAPO Radio suspends all broadcasts indefinitely
item.description: Management cites operational and technical reasons for the immediate halt without giving a return date.

item.title: Samia consults party leaders on reconciliation commission
item.description: Tanzania's main opposition party CHADEMA stayed away from talks on a body to coordinate constitutional reform.

item.title: Gunmen free 3 abducted Yei aid workers for $2,500 ransom
item.description: Three humanitarian staff seized along the Yei-Maridi Road were released after their captors received a cash payment.

item.title: Truck crash in Windhoek kills passenger after brake failure
item.description: A truck crashed into the College of the Arts theatre yard after its brakes failed, and police have opened a culpable homicide case.

item.title: NNPC probes fire at Lagos filling station
item.description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited has launched an investigation into a fire that engulfed a filling station in Lagos.

item.title: Uganda launches $17.7 billion energy compact
item.description: The government targets 85% electricity access and 50% clean cooking by 2030 under a new energy plan.

item.title: Aterian pinpoints four copper-silver targets in Botswana's Kalahari belt
item.description: Drone surveys and AI-assisted geophysics flagged favourable geological structures across a 20-kilometre licence corridor, though mineralisation is not yet confirmed.

item.title: Tanzania plans 100 standard neonatal units by 2028
item.description: The expansion would raise the national total of newborn care units from 438 to 538, Deputy Health Minister Florence Samizi said.

item.title: Kenya and EU conclude data talks
item.description: A deal allowing free data movement between Kenya and the EU is closer after two years of negotiations.

item.title: Zanzibar Second Vice-President orders swift justice for abuse cases
item.description: Hemed Suleiman Abdulla urged security authorities in Pemba to speed up investigations into sexual abuse, drug trafficking and theft.

item.title: Botswana banks remain resilient, council finds
item.description: The Financial Stability Council reported on November 11 that Botswana's financial system is sound and supports economic activity.

item.title: Algeria, Niger plan SME support for young trainees
item.description: A joint government initiative aims to link Algerian businesses with Nigerien graduates returning home.

item.title: CEMAC meets in Malabo to propose governance and funding reforms
item.description: Officials, experts and Technical Secretariat staff are reviewing how powers, programmes and resources are shared across the regional body.

item.title: Faculty of Medicine in Sousse hosts Sadok Besrour awards
item.description: Two researchers will receive 5,000 Canadian dollars each during the ceremony on Friday, 20 November 2026.

item.title: Ghana re-elected to ITU Council and wins Radio Regulations Board seat
item.description: Ghana's National Communications Authority director-general Edmund Yirenkyi Fianko polled 173 of 177 votes for a Radio Regulations Board seat.

item.title: Sirleaf warns Liberian leaders against threatening the country's peace
item.description: Former President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf urged those in power to pursue inclusion, equal opportunity and true unity to protect Liberia from a return to conflict.

item.title: Burundi league sees upsets as Vital'O FC falls
item.description: Vision FC, Never Give Up, Rukinzo, Inter Stars, Panthère Noire, and Musongati FC secured victories in a weekend of football action.

item.title: Singer Hage uses music to fight estate battle
item.description: Raquel Hage released a five-track EP to express frustration with the Liberian justice system over her mother's medical care.

item.title: Expert warns Dakar port wheat dispute could lift bread prices
item.description: A blockade of a wheat ship at Dakar's berth 4 has been in place since October 26, 2026, between Grands Moulins de Dakar and the new concessionaire Jambaar SA.

item.title: Liberia launches 285 machines for rural roads
item.description: President Boakai calls for maintenance amid public criticism over the procurement and cost of the heavy equipment.

item.title: LAZ vows legal action as youths plan march to scrap term limits
item.description: Over 60,000 young people from 10 provinces plan to march in Lusaka on November 25 to demand the removal of presidential term limits.

item.title: CCITF hosts transport and logistics forum in Tunis on Dec. 2
item.description: The French-Tunisian Chamber of Commerce and Industry gathers sector experts and officials to present a logistics study to 2040.

item.title: Chad launches free diabetes and blood pressure screening in N'Djamena
item.description: The five-day drive, which also introduces biometric patient enrolment, runs across several sites in the capital.

item.title: Liberia's Road Fund wins 2026 Builder Award
item.description: The National Road Fund received continental recognition for its leadership in sustainable road maintenance financing.

item.title: Liberia ports to operate 24 hours to cut costs
item.description: The government announced immediate relief measures including removal of shipping fees and customs bottlenecks to ease congestion.

item.title: Mutale-Nalumango urges private investment in refugee areas
item.description: Zambia's vice-president calls for business support to transform refugee settlements into economic hubs.

item.title: FAGACE opens Madagascar office to ease bank loans for small firms
item.description: The African guarantee fund can cover up to half of a loan, cutting the risk for lenders and easing collateral demands on borrowers.

item.title: Court sets December 16 to resume Esther Lungu theft trial
item.description: The Lusaka Magistrate's Court has barred any further adjournments, so the case must move forward on that date.

item.title: Burundi reforms Obuha to decentralize construction projects
item.description: A new decree will shift construction execution to communes and establish a director-general role, aiming to reduce currency pressure and improve project oversight.

item.title: Lilongwe City Council signs deal for 150 electric buses
item.description: The Memorandum of Understanding with Indian firm Mercury EV-Tech Limited also covers an electric vehicle assembly plant in the capital.

item.title: Ghana exports to China hit $290 million
item.description: China's zero-tariff policy boosted Ghanaian shipments to $290 million in June, with more market access expected.

item.title: Malawi's Chief Justice sends Speaker row to constitutional panel
item.description: Mkoka's challenge to 12 proposed parliamentary committees will now be heard by a panel of at least three High Court judges.

item.title: Corridor 13 project nears 85% road completion
item.description: The 168 billion CFA franc project funded by the African Development Bank includes ports, schools, health centers, and roads linking Congo, CAR, and Chad.

item.title: French view on Algeria's independence largely calm
item.description: Most French people see Algeria's independence as positive for both nations and support continued cooperation.

item.title: Ghana economy ranks eighth in Africa
item.description: President Mahama announced Ghana's Gross Domestic Product reached $114 billion in 2025, making it the second-largest economy in West Africa.

item.title: Fred and Andry crowned Madagascar rally champions for 2026
item.description: The brothers took the 46th Grand Rallye de Madagascar, the final stage of which was run in Moramanga from 13 to 15 November.

item.title: Malawi firms can now import their own diesel
item.description: The Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority (MERA) has opened applications for companies to import diesel directly for their operations.

item.title: Benin launches climate resilience project
item.description: The seven-billion CFA franc project will support rural populations in nine vulnerable communes facing ecological threats.

item.title: Mali activist Clément Dembélé marks three years in jail despite being cleared
item.description: A judge ordered his release several times, but the anti-cybercrime prosecutor opposed each order and the Supreme Court refused release in August.

item.title: Cameroon to issue CFAF 10.19 trillion in debt by 2031
item.description: Most of the borrowing will go toward repaying existing securities, leaving the government with limited room for new spending.

item.title: Nigerian stocks gain N351bn on Monday
item.description: The Nigerian Exchange Limited's All-Share Index rose 0.21 per cent to 252,809.78 points, with industrial, consumer goods and insurance stocks leading the gains.

item.title: ECOWAS and AfDB launch 500 million dollar rice project
item.description: The regional initiative aims to boost local rice production and reduce import dependency across 14 countries.

item.title: Eswatini U-23 AFCON dream ends in Algeria
item.description: Algeria defeated Eswatini 3-1 in the second leg, securing a 4-3 aggregate victory and ending Eswatini's hopes of reaching the continental finals.

item.title: Pupil, 14, drowns in Mbabane River after leaving school to swim
item.description: Police and fire rescue divers recovered the body of the Form I pupil from Hermann Gmeiner (SOS) High School several hours after the drowning was reported.

item.title: Togo adds Ewe and Kabye as optional BAC 2 subjects
item.description: Candidates for the June 2027 baccalaureate exam can now sit papers in two national languages, Ewe and Kabye.

item.title: Commodity prices surge in Damazin as military conflict spreads
item.description: Essential goods become scarce and household incomes dwindle as fighting expands to Bau locality.

item.title: Burkina Faso minister praises animal vaccination campaign
item.description: Minister Amadou Dicko oversaw a national animal vaccination and artificial insemination drive in Nazinon, Oubri, and Yaadga regions.

item.title: MINURSO contingent begins withdrawal from Laâyoune
item.description: The first contingent of the UN mission has started leaving following the expiration of its mandate on October 31, 2026.

item.title: Niger's communication regulator opens November session in Niamey
item.description: The National Communication Observatory (ONC) will examine draft rules on private audiovisual and electronic media, public access to state media and complaint handling.

item.title: Ivorian minister Nassénéba Touré receives Makeda Honorary Prize in Paris
item.description: Touré was honoured for her political career and her work on women's leadership and economic empowerment.

item.title: Lusaka construction worker wins K6,000,000 on betPawa
item.description: Davis, a construction worker, collected Zambia's largest recorded JetX win after four bets each paid the K1,500,000 maximum in one flight.

item.title: Dr Adama Sawadogo becomes Burkina Faso's first cardiovascular surgeon with agrégé rank
item.description: He won the rank of Maître de conférences agrégé at a continental competition held in Bangui, Central African Republic.

item.title: Burkina Faso, Nicaragua agree visa exemption
item.description: Diplomats from Burkina Faso and Nicaragua met on Monday to boost cooperation in agriculture, culture, and parliamentary exchanges.

item.title: Bobo-Dioulasso to host AFoodPack 5 packaging salon from November 27
item.description: The fifth edition of the African agro-food packaging salon will focus on ecological packaging for cashew, mango, sesame and shea producers.

item.title: Western Cape water allocations cut as dam storage drops
item.description: Water and Sanitation Minister Pemmy Majodina announced a 7% cut for domestic and industrial users and 15% for irrigation.

item.title: Senegal to submit third climate plan to UN soon, minister says
item.description: Environment Minister Aliou Gori Diouf said the validated NDC 3.0 will go in very shortly, ahead of COP32 in Ethiopia in 2027.

item.title: French justice minister to visit Morocco for talks
item.description: Gérald Darmanin will meet his Moroccan counterpart Abdellatif Ouahbi to discuss judicial cooperation and combatting crime.
